## 🌱 Getting Started

This course has lessons covering the fundamentals of building AI Agents. Each lesson covers its own topic so start wherever you like!

There is multi-language support for this course. Go to our [available languages here](#-multi-language-support). 

If this is your first time building with Generative AI models, check out our [Generative AI For Beginners](https://aka.ms/genai-beginners) course, which includes 21 lessons on building with GenAI.

Don't forget to [star (🌟) this repo](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/exploring-projects-on-github/saving-repositories-with-stars?WT.mc_id=academic-105485-koreyst) and [fork this repo](https://github.com/microsoft/ai-agents-for-beginners/fork) to run the code.

### Meet Other Learners, Get Your Questions Answered

If you get stuck or have any questions about building AI Agents, join our dedicated Discord Channel in the [Microsoft Foundry Discord](https://aka.ms/ai-agents/discord).

### What You Need 

Each lesson in this course includes code examples, which can be found in the code_samples folder. You can [fork this repo](https://github.com/microsoft/ai-agents-for-beginners/fork) to create your own copy.  

The code examples in these exercises utilize Microsoft Agent Framework with Microsoft Foundry Agent Service V2:

- [Microsoft Foundry](https://aka.ms/ai-agents-beginners/ai-foundry) - Azure Account Required

This course uses the following AI Agent frameworks and services from Microsoft:

- [Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF)](https://learn.microsoft.com/agent-framework/overview/)
- [Microsoft Foundry Agent Service V2](https://aka.ms/ai-agents-beginners/ai-agent-service)

Some code samples also support alternative OpenAI-compatible providers such as [MiniMax](https://platform.minimaxi.com/), which offers large-context models (up to 204K tokens). See the [Course Setup](./00-course-setup/README.md) for configuration details.

For more information on running the code for this course, go to the [Course Setup](./00-course-setup/README.md).

## 🙏 Want to help?

Do you have suggestions or found spelling or code errors? [Raise an issue](https://github.com/microsoft/ai-agents-for-beginners/issues?WT.mc_id=academic-105485-koreyst) or [Create a pull request](https://github.com/microsoft/ai-agents-for-beginners/pulls?WT.mc_id=academic-105485-koreyst)



## 📂 Each lesson includes

- A written lesson located in the README and a short video
- Python code samples using Microsoft Agent Framework with Microsoft Foundry
- Links to extra resources to continue your learning

aiSummary.oneLiner: A step-by-step curriculum teaching the fundamentals of building autonomous AI agents.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: This project delivers a comprehensive educational curriculum focused specifically on the design, architecture, and implementation of autonomous AI agents. It progresses from basic conceptual understanding to complex multi-agent systems using frameworks like AutoGen and Semantic Kernel. The repository includes theoretical explanations, interactive Jupyter notebooks, and complete codebase examples. It emphasizes practical application, showing how agents can be equipped with tools to interact with external APIs and databases. The course is designed to help developers transition from simple chat applications to sophisticated, task-oriented AI systems.
keyFeatures: Progressive curriculum: Structures learning from basic agent concepts to advanced multi-agent orchestration.
Microsoft framework integration: Includes practical code samples leveraging the Microsoft Agent Framework and Foundry Agent Service.
Tool usage tutorials: Teaches how to equip agents with the ability to execute code and call external APIs.
Interactive notebooks: Includes Jupyter notebooks for hands-on experimentation with agent logic.
Architecture patterns: Details established patterns for agent memory, planning, and reflection.

useCases.title: Learning agent architecture
useCases.description: Developers follow the course to understand how to build systems where AI plans and executes multi-step tasks.

useCases.title: Building task automations
useCases.description: Engineers learn to create agents that can automatically research topics and summarize findings.

useCases.title: Multi-agent coordination
useCases.description: Teams study the advanced lessons to build systems where specialized agents collaborate to solve complex problems.

useCases.title: Tool integration
useCases.description: Programmers learn how to safely expose their internal business APIs to autonomous agents.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Software developers and AI enthusiasts who want to learn how to build agentic systems. It assumes a basic understanding of programming and general Large Language Model concepts.
